bulletin.title: Advisories
bulletin.lede: MOMUS reads CISA KEV, OSV and GHSA. This is what it publishes back, in the same shape — so the same tooling can read us.
bulletin.disclosure_note: An open advisory carries no reproducer, no evidence and no target. MOMUS audits services we operate, so a working reproducer for an unfixed hole would be an attack script published under our own name. A fixed advisory carries everything: it is a lesson now, not a weapon.
bulletin.disclosure_line_fixed: Full disclosure — this issue is fixed.
bulletin.disclosure_line_open: Withheld pending a fix — no reproducer, no evidence, no target.
bulletin.disclosure_line_withdrawn: Withdrawn — the entry stays on the record; the technical detail does not.
bulletin.pin_note: The index is Ed25519-signed over the RFC 8785 canonical form of {advisories, timestamp} — the same envelope ARGUS's WARDEN already verifies, and the same key MOMUS signs its findings with. Fetch the signed index to check it yourself.
bulletin.reproducer_withheld: Withheld until a MOMUS-signed fixed verdict exists. This component is one we operate.
bulletin.reproducer_withdrawn: Withheld: MOMUS no longer stands behind this advisory, so it must not carry a working reproducer under MOMUS's signature.
bulletin.empty_disabled: This deployment does not publish a bulletin — advisory publishing is off, so there is no record here to read.
bulletin.empty_offline: The bulletin could not be reached ({{message}}), so this page cannot tell you what is on the record — which is not the same as the record being empty.
bulletin.empty_none: MOMUS has published no advisories yet. An empty record means nothing has been published — not that nothing has been found.

how.heading: Safe, read-only probes against our own components
how.intro_scope: MOMUS attacks the ecosystem’s own oracles, hub and settlement paths — never third parties.
how.intro_proof: Every probe is non-destructive; every result is emitted as an {{finding}} with a reproducer, so the claim carries its own proof.
how.probe_authz_body: Pushes an oracle's free-tier limits to confirm the ceiling actually holds — that a metered capability can't be coaxed into serving beyond its unpaid quota.
how.probe_integrity_body: Tampers with a copy of a manifest or work-receipt and checks that verification fails closed — a forged or mutated document must never validate.
how.probe_settlement_body: Attempts unpaid-serve, double-spend and out-of-order settlement against escrow gates to prove funds never move without a verified verdict.
how.probe_injection_body: Feeds instruction-shaped payloads into LLM-backed nodes to confirm they treat fetched content as untrusted data, never as commands.
how.probe_replay_body: Replays nonces and stale requests to check that duplicate-guards and freshness windows reject a re-sent, already-settled invocation.
how.probe_dos_body: Sends over-max and malformed shapes to confirm resource ceilings and input validation refuse work that would exhaust the node.

keys.diagram_aria: Key separation: Scanner signs a finding; independent verifiers confirm; a separate Treasury key releases the payout.
keys.momus_side_note: MOMUS side — finds & signs, cannot pay

learn.title: It gets sharper every scan
learn.intro: MOMUS ingests public security reports from allowlisted feeds and learns from its own and its peers’ confirmed findings. A UCB bandit over attack-classes decides which probes to run first — spending effort where it has recently paid off, while still exploring the quiet corners.
learn.untrusted_data_body: Fetched reports are treated as data behind a prompt-firewall. A CVE write-up can teach MOMUS which class of bug to look for; it can never tell MOMUS what to do. Distillation maps each report to attack categories — nothing more.
learn.bandit_priority_note: Higher score = probed sooner. Live values appear in the panel’s intelligence widget once the backend is reachable.

llm.heading: Bring your own cognition
llm.intro_provider_agnostic: The reasoning behind a probe is provider-agnostic.
llm.intro_any_provider: Point MOMUS at a hosted frontier model, a local runtime, or the ecosystem’s own {{metis}} tier — or run the {{offline}} mode with no network at all.

pays.cannot_pay_itself_title: MOMUS is structurally unable to pay itself
pays.guarantee_scanner_key_only_body: MOMUS holds a single Ed25519 scanner key. It can sign a finding — it cannot sign a payout. /health surfaces holds_treasury_key:false so the separation is verifiable from outside.
pays.guarantee_independent_verification_body: A finding pays out only after independent confirmation: ≥2 distinct verifier keys for high/critical, one of which must be a registered external verifier such as Metis.
pays.guarantee_anti_griefing_deposit_body: Submitting for bounty requires a deposit, so flooding the queue with junk findings costs the sender — not the Treasury.
pays.guarantee_dedup_replay_guard_body: A stable dedup_key is the identity of the bug, not the report. Rediscovering one flaw collapses to a single payable claim — you cannot get paid twice.
pays.guarantee_fail_closed_crypto_off_body: With the crypto master switch off, no settlement path exists. Payouts don't silently succeed — they simply cannot happen.
pays.lede: A red team that signs its own cheques is a fraud generator. So the role that FINDS and the role that PAYS are split across separate keys in separate containers — with independent verifiers wedged between them.

treasury.heading: The payer is a different service, with a different key
treasury.separation_intro: MOMUS finds and signs. It cannot pay itself — a separate {{treasury}} holds the only key that can release a bounty, in its own container with its own key volume. Don't take that on faith: the two keys below are read live from two different services.
treasury.treasury_key_role: releases bounties · ❌ cannot find or verify
treasury.verdict_offline: Treasury not reachable from here — the separation still holds in the service topology.
treasury.verdict_keys_distinct: ✓ Verified live: the two keys are different. No single key can both declare a finding valid and release its payout.
treasury.verdict_keys_identical: ⚠ The two keys look identical — that would be a misconfiguration (the Treasury refuses to start in this state).
treasury.public_endpoints_note: Only {{health}} and {{ledger}} are public. The payout path stays private — the one service that can release money does not get an open endpoint.
